evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
evidence.text: The entry gives the current reading míng and meanings including a person’s name, a thing’s designation, reputation, and the verb sense “to refer to, describe.” This supports learner wording such as “name” and “to name/designate.”
evidence.title: 名 — 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》2021

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: standard form, current component layout, and received Shuowen explanation
evidence.text: The entry labels 名 as the standard form, assigns it to 口部, and describes its regular-script form as upper 夕 and lower 口. It separately records the Shuowen explanation: self-designation, from 口 and 夕, with 夕 glossed as darkness. This supports describing the visible current split while identifying the night account as a received explanation.
evidence.title: [A00508] 名 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Institute of History and Philology, Ancient Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: historical form stages and received component account
evidence.text: The page lists oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal, and Shuowen forms and identifies the upper part as 夕 and lower as 口. It presents the night-identification account as the explanation of both parts; this records a received interpretation, not independent proof of original motivation.
evidence.title: 漢字「名」：字形演變

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: 夕 and 名 component accounts; reported uses
evidence.text: The 夕 discussion says its basic sense is the sunset and moonrise interval, sometimes extended to night, and describes 夕 and 月 as graphically differentiated. For 名, the entry attributes the night-identification analysis to Xu Shen, reports an oracle-bone place-name token 《乙》3290, a Western Zhou naming use on the 少虡 sword, a bronze use glossed 銘, and Warring States manuscript uses. These examples record different contexts but do not establish a continuous semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 夕 (includes 名 entry)

search_audit.query: Wikimedia Commons exact 名 oracle and Western Zhou bronze glyph files
search_audit.outcome: Opened exact file description pages, inspected their captions/source labels/licensing and extracted the original-file links. Both are modern vector redrawings stated to be public domain.

gaps: The received 夕 + 口 night-identification account is well documented as a historical explanation, but inspected sources do not independently establish that it was the graph’s original motivation.

The reported oracle-bone place-name token does not resolve the earliest token’s precise semantics or date; the cited records also do not establish a continuous chronology among name, naming, inscription, reputation, and status senses.
Commons file pages establish provenance and rights, but I did not inspect the image pixels in this invocation; the separate visual stage should verify their visible details.
No direct independent primary paleographic argument for the reported alternative phonetic analysis was located in this research pass.
